faqs.question: What does Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method measure?
faqs.answer: Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method examines the characteristics of nipple discharge viz. cellular composition, including the presence of abnormal cells, inflammatory cells, or other pathological features.

faqs.question: Why is Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method done?
faqs.answer: Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method is done for several reasons, including: • To investigate the cause of nipple discharge • To diagnose and monitor breast conditions, such as breast cancer, infection, and hormonal changes • To evaluate the effectiveness of treatment for breast conditions

faqs.question: When is Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method may be recommended if you have • Spontaneous nipple discharge without any stimulation. • Bloodstained or abnormal-colored nipple discharge. • A lump or mass in the breast. • A family history of breast cancer or other breast conditions.

faqs.question: What if the results of Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method are abnormal?
faqs.answer: If the results of Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method are abnormal, it may indicate various conditions, including: • Infection, such as mastitis • Benign breast conditions like fibroadenoma • Precancerous changes in the breast tissue It is important to discuss your test results with your doctor for further evaluation and appropriate management.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method?
faqs.answer: During the Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method: • A sample of nipple discharge will be collected using a special technique. • The sample will be examined under a microscope to evaluate its characteristics. • The test is quick and relatively painless, although it may cause slight discomfort.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method?
faqs.answer: To prepare for Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method: • Inform your doctor about any medications you are taking, including hormonal supplements. • Avoid applying creams, ointments, or powders to the nipple area before the test. • Follow any additional instructions provided by your doctor. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method include: • Mammogram: A breast X-ray that helps detect any abnormalities in the breast tissue. • Breast Ultrasound: Uses sound waves to create images of the breast tissue and can help determine if the discharge is related to a mass or cyst. • Biopsy: A procedure to collect a small tissue sample for further examination.

faqs.question: What is Nipple Discharge by Conventional Method also known as?
What is nipple discharge?
faqs.answer: Nipple discharge refers to any fluid that comes out from the nipple. It can vary in colour, consistency, and amount. While nipple discharge can sometimes occur naturally, it may also be a sign of an underlying condition such as infection or breast cancer.
